title: Safe prefix-aware eviction and visibility guarantees for GPU-resident KV cache
creator: Maya Singh
description: Design and implement a correctness-first eviction subsystem for the GPU-resident KV cache that supports mixed LRU/TTL/priority and prefix-aware policies while preserving read-after-evict semantics for in-flight continuous batching. The goal is to eliminate rare correctness bugs observed under heavy tail load (inference spikes + long prefix reuse), bound GPU memory usage, and provide observable invariants and automated checks. This ticket covers design, prototype, bench verification, and a gated rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction design approved by runtime and infra leads (doc + annotated invariants)
Implementation provides atomic visibility guarantees: once a key is evicted, no request may observe a stale KV entry even if that request started before eviction completed
Support for prefix-aware pinning counts and per-prefix TTL that interact deterministically with size-based LRU evictions
Microbench shows <2% tail-latency regressions for typical continuous-batching workloads and GPU memory usage bounded under target configurations
E2E tests (simulated multi-worker continuous batching) detect and assert invariants; CI gate added
Metrics shipped: eviction_rate, eviction_failures, prefix_refcounts, kv_version_mismatch_count, eviction_lag_ms
tasks: Write design doc describing two-phase eviction (mark->drain->remove) and per-prefix reference counting
Prototype per-key versioning and eviction fence primitives in runtime core
Integrate GPU staging buffer to avoid spikes during bulk evictions
Add CI stress test harness that simulates continuous batching + concurrent writes and long-lived prefix reuse
Benchmark memory/latency on p4d and a100 clusters and collect dashboards
Gradual rollout plan with canary and rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-21: Initial spike: Prod incident 2026-02-20 revealed rare incorrect generations when KV entries were evicted during long-lived stream generations. Related to ENG-5824 investigations.
2026-02-25: Design draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Eviction+Safeguards (see section 'mark-drain-remove' and atomic fences)

2026-03-02: Architecture review with @Eva Romero and @Liam Chen. Primary concerns: cost of per-key versioning and GPU copying overhead. Agreed to prototype lightweight 24-bit version counters and avoid host<->gpu roundtrips on hot paths.

2026-03-05: Benchmarks (internal/perf/kv-evict-2) show base throughput drop of ~0.9% with version checks; tail P99 increased 1.3ms on p4d with naive eviction. After adding GPU staging buffer, tail regressed <0.4ms. See dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/kv-evictions/eviction-experiments
2026-03-08: PR opened implementing eviction fence and per-prefix reference counts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345. Needs review from storage owner and runtime perf.

2026-03-09: Perf review notes from @Jia Park: recommended using a bit-packed header on KV entries to store version + pinned flag to reduce memory overhead. Also suggested sampling-based TTL enforcement to reduce scan cost.

2026-03-10: Updated design to use LRU buckets with per-bucket watermarks and prefix reference counters. Added invariant asserts in debug builds that will fail CI on mismatch. Plan to run canary for 48 hours on dedicated-dev fleet.
notes: Design decision: prefer deterministic two-phase eviction over opportunistic immediate reclaim to guarantee read-after-evict correctness for streaming requests that may hold references into the KV cache during continuous batching.

Trade-off: per-key versioning increases metadata by ~8-12 bytes per entry; we mitigate by packing flags and using 3-byte roll-over safe counters. This was preferred to more expensive global quiesce operations.
Rollback criteria for rollout: if kv_version_mismatch_count > 10/min for 15 minutes on canary, auto-disable prefix-aware eviction and fall back to existing LRU TTL policy.
Follow-ups: explore hybrid TTL eviction with probabilistic early-decay to reduce scanning cost, and consider async background compaction for very large prefixes.
Related tickets: ENG-5824 (prefix eviction guarantees), ENG-9407 (adaptive prefix pinning). This ticket coordinates to unify guarantees and avoid duplicate mechanisms.
